---
title: "Renaming Data Objects"
---

In this notebook we collect all previously processed data objects and rename them, before saving to folder data.

# Preliminaries

Load the packages used in this notebook:
```{r load packages}
library(dplyr) # A Grammar of Data Manipulation
library(glue) # Interpreted String Literals
library(here) # A Simpler Way to Find Your Files
library(stringr)
library(usethis)
```

## Tracts

Load, rename and save tract data frames. These are sf objects with the geometry of the census tracts, plus bonus socio-economic and demographic data.

Read files with the tract data:
```{r}
file_names <- data.frame(object = list.files(path = "intermediate-data-objects/", pattern = "_walksheds_df.rda"))
```

Mutate to obtain the name of the city:
```{r}
file_names <- file_names |>
  mutate(city = stringr::str_remove(object, pattern = "_walksheds_df.rda"))
```

Load, rename, and save:
```{r}
for(i in 1:nrow(file_names)){
  load(glue::glue("intermediate-data-objects/{file_names$object[i]}"))
  new_name <- glue::glue("{file_names$city[i]}_tracts")
  assign(new_name, walksheds_df)
  do.call("use_data", list(as.name(new_name), overwrite = TRUE))
}
```

## Walksheds

Load, rename and save wa;kshed data frames. These are sf objects with the geometry of the walksheds.

Read files with the tract data:
```{r}
file_names <- data.frame(object = list.files(path = "intermediate-data-objects/", pattern = "_walksheds.rda"))
```

Mutate to obtain the name of the city:
```{r}
file_names <- file_names |>
  mutate(city = stringr::str_remove(object, pattern = "_walksheds.rda"))
```

Load, rename, and save:
```{r}
for(i in 1:nrow(file_names)){
  load(glue::glue("intermediate-data-objects/{file_names$object[i]}"))
  new_name <- glue::glue("{file_names$city[i]}_walksheds")
  assign(new_name, walksheds)
  do.call("use_data", list(as.name(new_name), overwrite = TRUE))
}
```
